rows.name: CABAL_INSTALL
rows.who_sets: `flake.nix` in the Nix dev shell, and the CI workflows.
rows.read_by: `make` in `ingest`, `cmake`, the ingest Python tools and CI scripts (`ingest/Makefile`, `ingest/CMakeLists.txt`, `ingest/build-model.py` and 7 more files)
rows.values: Name or path of the `cabal` program (the Haskell build tool). The readers use the text as a command name without a check. `make CABAL_INSTALL=value` also works in `ingest/Makefile`.
rows.default: Unset: `ingest/Makefile`, the Python tools and `bin/ci/install-sydtest-discover.sh` run `cabal`. Empty: only the Python tools differ. They use the empty text as the command.
rows.effect: Selects the `cabal` program for the ingest Haskell code. `ingest/Makefile` runs it for the targets `test` and `test-coverage`. `ingest/build-model.py` and `tron_ingest_tools` use it to run ingest only when no pre-built ingest executable is given.
rows.notes: In `ingest/CMakeLists.txt`, `find_program` lists the value after the name `cabal`. A program with a listed name wins over the value. When `IN_NIX_SHELL` is not set, CMake lists `cabal-3.16.0.0` first and stops unless the found program reports version 3.16.0.0.

rows.name: CLANG_RESOURCE_DIR
rows.who_sets: `flake.nix`, for the Nix dev shell and the Nix CMake builds.
rows.read_by: Nothing in TRON. `flake.nix` exports it in the Nix dev shell and in the Nix CMake builds (`tron-cmake-test-build`, `cmake-sandbox`).
rows.values: Directory path in the Nix store: `${llvm19.clang}/resource-root`. On macOS the Nix dev shell sets empty text.
rows.default: Unset: nothing changes. No file in the repository reads this name.
rows.effect: Nothing changes in TRON. No file in the repository reads this name.

rows.name: CMAKE_CXX_COMPILER
rows.read_by: Nothing in TRON. `flake.nix` exports it in the Nix dev shell.
rows.values: Path of the `clang++-19` wrapper program in the Nix store.
rows.default: Unset: nothing changes. No file in the repository reads the environment variable.
rows.effect: Nothing changes in TRON. No file in the repository reads the environment variable. `CMakePresets.json` sets the CMake cache variable of the same name to `clang++-19`, and that is a separate setting.
rows.notes: The Nix dev shell also sets `CXX` to the same path.

rows.name: CMAKE_C_COMPILER
rows.read_by: Nothing in TRON. `flake.nix` exports it in the Nix dev shell.
rows.values: Path of the `clang-19` wrapper program in the Nix store.
rows.default: Unset: nothing changes. No file in the repository reads the environment variable.
rows.effect: Nothing changes in TRON. No file in the repository reads the environment variable. `CMakePresets.json` sets the CMake cache variable of the same name to `clang-19`, and that is a separate setting.
rows.notes: The Nix dev shell also sets `CC` to the same path.

rows.name: CMAKE_DEFINES
rows.values: Any text. `GNUmakefile` only prints it. `make CMAKE_DEFINES=value` also works.
rows.effect: Nothing changes in the build. When `DEBUG` is set, `make` prints the line `CMAKE_DEFINES = <value>` while it parses `GNUmakefile`. No rule passes the value to CMake.

rows.name: COMPILER_RT_BUILTINS_ROOT
rows.who_sets: `flake.nix`, for the Nix dev shell and the Nix CMake builds.
rows.values: Directory path. CMake searches it for the library `clang_rt.builtins-x86_64`. The Nix files set `${llvm19.compiler-rt}/lib/linux`.
rows.effect: CMake searches this directory for the compiler-rt builtins library before `/usr/lib/llvm-19/lib/clang/19/lib/linux`. CMake links the library that it finds into libtron. Configure stops with the error `clang_rt.builtins-x86_64 library not found` when neither directory holds the library.
rows.notes: `find_library` uses `NO_DEFAULT_PATH`. CMake searches no other directory. CMake keeps the result in the cache variable `COMPILER_RT_BUILTINS`. A build tree that already holds a result does not search again.

rows.name: DEBUG
rows.values: `GNUmakefile`: any non-empty text counts as set, `0` included. `bin/iotools-1.5/Makefile`: `0` selects the optimised build, and any other text selects the debug build. `make DEBUG=1` also works.
rows.default: Unset: `GNUmakefile` prints no extra lines. `bin/iotools-1.5/Makefile` uses `1`, the debug build with `-O0 -ggdb`.
rows.effect: `GNUmakefile` prints the values of `BUILD_TYPE`, `MAKEFLAGS`, `TESTS`, `PHONY`, `RUN` and `CMAKE_DEFINES` while it parses, and changes nothing else. In `bin/iotools-1.5/Makefile` (the makefile of iotools, a third-party I/O tool copied into the repository), `0` compiles with `-O2 -DNDEBUG`.
rows.notes: The two makefiles use the same name for different purposes. A `DEBUG` that is exported for another tool also turns on the `GNUmakefile` output. No TRON build file runs the iotools makefile.

rows.name: ENABLE_FUSE_STATS
rows.who_sets: Developers who build without FUSE stats.
rows.values: Text for the CMake option `ENABLE_FUSE_STATS`, for example `ON` or `OFF`. The makefile passes the text without a check. `make ENABLE_FUSE_STATS=OFF` also works.
rows.default: Unset: `ON`. Empty: the makefile keeps the empty text and passes it to CMake.
rows.effect: Selects at CMake configure time whether the FUSE stats feature is compiled. `GNUmakefile` passes it to `cmake` as `-DENABLE_FUSE_STATS=<value>`. A changed value rewrites the file `gen/.fuse_stats_stamp`, and `make` then runs CMake configure again.
rows.notes: When `REMOTE` sends the build to an LSF worker, `bin/bsub-build` copies a non-empty environment value into the job. A value on the `make` command line also travels with the job.

evidence.quote: option(ENABLE_FUSE_STATS "Enable FUSE filesystem stats feature" ON)
for var in ENABLE_FUSE_STATS CCACHE_DISABLE XDG_CACHE_HOME; do

rows.name: FUSE_STATS_STAMP
rows.values: File path. This is an internal make variable. `GNUmakefile` assigns it and ignores an environment value, except when the only goals are `list-tests` or `list-tests-core`.
rows.default: Unset: `gen/.fuse_stats_stamp`. When the only goals are `list-tests` or `list-tests-core`, the text is empty.
rows.effect: An environment value changes no build result. For the goals `list-tests` and `list-tests-core` alone, `make` puts the value into the prerequisite lists of the CMake configure targets and the package target. `make` does not build those targets for these goals.
rows.notes: The file holds the last `ENABLE_FUSE_STATS` value. A changed file makes `make` run CMake configure again. `make FUSE_STATS_STAMP=path` on the command line replaces the path for every goal.

rows.name: HAS_AVX512
rows.values: Only the text `no` has an effect. On Linux the makefile assigns `yes` or `no` itself and ignores an environment value. On macOS it uses the environment value.
rows.default: Unset: on Linux, `yes` when `/proc/cpuinfo` lists the flag `avx512f`, otherwise `no`. On macOS, empty text.
rows.effect: The value `no` marks a build host whose CPU has no AVX-512 (a CPU instruction set). `make t_<name>` then builds the test and stops with an error before the run. With `REMOTE` at `0`, the Slice test targets and `test-proxy` also stop with an error.
rows.notes: `make HAS_AVX512=value` on the command line replaces the detected value on Linux too. The `-old` test targets stop in the same way. The sanitizer and coverage targets do not check the variable.

evidence.quote: HAS_AVX512 := $(shell grep -q avx512f /proc/cpuinfo 2>/dev/null && echo yes || echo no)
@echo "Error: Cannot run $@: cross-compiled for AVX-512. Run tests on a machine with AVX-512." >&2; exit 1

rows.name: INGEST_PYTHON_VERSION
rows.who_sets: Nobody by default. Developers may override it.
rows.values: A Python version that `uv` (the Python package tool) accepts for `--python`, for example `3.12.7`. The makefile does not check it. `make INGEST_PYTHON_VERSION=value` also works.
rows.default: Unset: the value of `TOKENIZER_PYTHON_VERSION`, `3.12.7` by default. Empty: the makefile keeps the empty text, and `--python` gets no version.
rows.effect: Selects the Python version of the two ingest environments, `ingest/export/.venv` and `ingest/runtime/.venv`. The target `ingest-deps` passes it to `uv sync --frozen --python`.
rows.notes: When `IN_NIX_SHELL` is set, `ingest-deps` skips `uv` and the value has no effect. A comment in `GNUmakefile` says that without `--python`, `uv sync` uses the newest Python of the host.

rows.name: LLVM_LIB_DIR
rows.who_sets: `flake.nix`, for the Nix dev shell and the Nix CMake builds.
rows.read_by: Nothing in TRON. `flake.nix` exports it in the Nix dev shell and in the Nix CMake builds (`tron-cmake-test-build`, `cmake-sandbox`).
rows.values: Directory path in the Nix store: `${llvm19.compiler-rt}/lib`. On macOS the Nix dev shell sets empty text.
rows.default: Unset: nothing changes. No file in the repository reads this name.
rows.effect: Nothing changes in TRON. No file in the repository reads this name.
rows.notes: A comment in `flake.nix` says that the value is for `CMakeLists.txt`. `CMakeLists.txt` reads `COMPILER_RT_BUILTINS_ROOT` and not this name.

evidence.quote: # Provide compiler-rt builtins path for CMakeLists.txt (Linux only)

rows.name: NPROC_BUILD
rows.who_sets: CI workflows, the Nix build and `bin/bsub-build`.
rows.values: Positive integer, a number of parallel jobs. `GNUmakefile` passes the text to `-j` without a check. `bin/ci/ci-select-tron-build-jobs.sh` accepts only digits with no leading `0`. `make NPROC_BUILD=4` also works.
rows.default: Unset: `GNUmakefile` uses the smaller of 16 jobs and the `nproc` output. `bin/ci/ci-select-tron-build-jobs.sh` stops with the error `NPROC_BUILD is required`.
rows.effect: `GNUmakefile` adds `-j <value>` to the flags of `make` and to its `cmake --build` commands, except the one that builds IWYU (the include-what-you-use tool). In the Nix build `tron-cmake-test-build`, the job count is the smaller of `NIX_BUILD_CORES` and this value.
rows.notes: When `REMOTE` sends the build to an LSF worker, `bin/bsub-build` exports it there with the value of `REMOTE_BUILD_CORES`. Two CI workflows and `nix/cmake-tron-test-build.nix` set 16 jobs. A comment in `GNUmakefile` says that `nproc` obeys `OMP_THREAD_LIMIT`.

evidence.quote: NPROC_BUILD := $(shell n=$$(nproc 2>/dev/null || echo 16); echo $$(( n < 16 ? n : 16 )))

rows.name: PRESET_STAMP
rows.values: File path. This is an internal make variable. `GNUmakefile` assigns it and ignores an environment value, except when the only goals are `list-tests` or `list-tests-core`.
rows.default: Unset: `gen/.preset_stamp`. When the only goals are `list-tests` or `list-tests-core`, the text is empty.
rows.effect: An environment value changes no build result. For the goals `list-tests` and `list-tests-core` alone, `make` puts the value into the prerequisite lists of the CMake configure targets. `make` does not build those targets for these goals.
rows.notes: The file holds the last CMake preset name, `native` or `darwin`. A changed file makes `make` run CMake configure again. `make PRESET_STAMP=path` on the command line replaces the path for every goal.

rows.name: REMOTE
rows.who_sets: Developers, in the shell or on the `make` command line.
rows.values: Exactly one of `0`, `1`, `sku0`, `sku1`. Spaces around the value are removed. Any other text stops `make` with an error. `make REMOTE=1` also works.
rows.default: Unset: the value of `TRON_REMOTE_EXECUTION` (default `0`) for build goals and test goals, and `0` for other goals. Empty: `make` stops with an error.
rows.effect: `0` runs everything on the local host. `1`, `sku0` and `sku1` send the build goals to an LSF worker through `bin/bsub-build`. They also add `--remote` to `bin/slice run` for `test`, `test-core`, `test-host`, `test-fpga` and `test-fast`.
rows.notes: `sku0` and `sku1` also add `--remote-sku=<value>`, a server class for the test run. With `1`, `sku0` or `sku1`, `make` stops with an error for goals that run tests directly, for example `run`, `t_<name>`, `test-proxy` and the coverage goals.

evidence.quote: $(error $(REMOTE_MODE_SOURCE) must be one of 0, 1, sku0, or sku1)
all build core build-core build-prod build-test build-ingest build-test-host build-test-fpga:

rows.name: REMOTE_BUILD_CORES
rows.read_by: `bin/bsub-build`, the script that submits a build to an LSF worker (`bin/bsub-build`)
rows.values: Positive integer, a number of cores. Text with a character other than a digit, or the text `0`, stops the script with exit code 2.
rows.effect: Sets the number of cores that the LSF build job reserves. The script exports the same number on the worker as `NPROC_BUILD` and `CARGO_BUILD_JOBS`. It also sets the default of `REMOTE_BUILD_MEM`, 8192 MB for each core.
rows.notes: When `REMOTE` sends the build to an LSF worker, `make -jN` overrides this variable with N. With GNU make 4.3, the makefile detects `-jN` only when N differs from `NPROC_BUILD`. A leading `0` passes the check, and the memory default reads the value as octal.

evidence.quote: echo "bsub-build: $2 must be a positive integer, got '$1'" >&2

rows.name: REMOTE_BUILD_MEM
rows.who_sets: Developers, before a build on an LSF worker.
rows.read_by: `bin/bsub-build`, the script that submits a build to an LSF worker (`bin/bsub-build`)
rows.values: A number of MB (megabytes). The script does not check the text. It passes the text to `bsub` in `rusage[mem=<value>]`.
rows.default: Unset: 8192 MB for each core of `REMOTE_BUILD_CORES`. That is 131072 MB (128 GB) for the default of 16 cores.
rows.effect: Sets the memory that the LSF build job reserves.
rows.notes: The script treats the number as MB. Its comment says `8 GB per core` for 8192, and its log line adds the suffix `M`. The repository holds no LSF configuration that confirms the unit of `rusage[mem=]`.

evidence.quote: # 8 GB per core. The generated models_*.cpp units cost 5-6 GB in a single

rows.name: REMOTE_BUILD_QUEUE
rows.who_sets: Developers, before a build on an LSF worker.
rows.read_by: `bin/bsub-build`, the script that submits a build to an LSF worker (`bin/bsub-build`)
rows.values: Name of an LSF queue. The script passes the text to `bsub -q` without a check.
rows.effect: Selects the LSF queue that receives the build job.

new_terms.definition: The script that submits a build command to an LSF worker and streams the output back. `make` runs it for build goals when `REMOTE` is `1`, `sku0` or `sku1`.
Two server classes of the remote test pool. `REMOTE=sku0` or `REMOTE=sku1` selects one for the test run. A build treats both as `1`.
The Haskell build tool that builds, runs and tests ingest.
The Python package tool that creates the Python environments outside the Nix dev shell.
A CPU instruction set. Every TRON build compiles for it, also on a host whose CPU does not have it.
A third-party I/O tool. A copy is in `bin/iotools-1.5`. No TRON build file builds it.
include-what-you-use, the tool that checks the include lines of C++ files.
The Nix derivation `tron-cmake-test-build`, the check `cmake-sandbox-configure` and the dev shell `cmake-sandbox`. All three take their environment from `cmakeSandboxEnvironment` in `flake.nix`.

notes: FUSE_STATS_STAMP, PRESET_STAMP and HAS_AVX512 are internal make variables. They stay as rows with drop false: the environment reaches make on one path each (the goals list-tests and list-tests-core alone, or macOS). INGEST_PYTHON_VERSION is in group make, as only GNUmakefile reads it. The input said NPROC_BUILD reaches every cmake --build of GNUmakefile. The IWYU build line has no -j, and the row says so. Some evidence quotes hold a pipe character, as the source lines do (GNUmakefile:96, GNUmakefile:245). doc/slice.md says that REMOTE=1 does not move make build*. GNUmakefile sends the build goals to bin/bsub-build. Checked outside the checkout with scratch files (GNU Make 4.3, CMake 3.22.1, bash): an empty environment value counts as unset for ifndef and is kept by ?=, a command-line value replaces a := assignment, and find_program tries an ENV value in NAMES after the listed names.
